All participants completed the vicarious optimism task for themselves and a friend.
The lists of events did not include very rare or very common events, and participants were told that the average likelihood was never lower than 3% or higher than 77%.
In the self condition, participants were asked to estimate the likelihood of negative life events happening to themselves.

In the friend condition, participants were asked to estimate the likelihood of negative life events happening to a friend with the same gender, age, and ethnicity as themselves (participants were asked to enter the name of the friend into a text box prior to starting the trials).
On each trial, a negative life event was presented, and participants were asked to imagine this event happening to themselves or their friend.
Participants were told that they would then see the actual average likelihood of this event happening to someone with similar demographic criteria to themselves or their friend.

Finally, participants were asked to again indicate the percentage likelihood of the negative event happening to themselves or their friend; they were instructed to indicate what they thought at that moment, regardless of what they entered previously.
